additional_info.subject: ID0455830-DC/Si-D/IE-[multi] Charging session failed CRM:03056000207
additional_info.body:
Hello Colin, good afternoon. I hope you are doing well.
I apologise for the lack of response in time as our system did not recognize the 170003302 as an SLA asset.
Jason is already working with the responsible to find what is the issue related to that. For the moment I recommend you to use the 170003301 as the asset reported, as this one is confirmed for SLA.
Moving on to the charging sessions:
3301 - 12:30 to 13:05:
As you can see, after the EV reached the 80% SoC, it stopped requesting Current (EV_TarCur[A]), it goes from 76A to 0A in a matter of miliseconds, and at the end it is reported, by our SECC, that the one that requested the stop was indeed the vehicle itself.
This looks like a constrain in the EV where the battery is limited to 80% to avoid damaging it further.
We recommend consulting with the manufacturer or the customer if it's possible to increase this from the vehicle.
For the charger 3303 - 12:48:
My assumption here is that the 2 times that the customer tried to charge, he use the charger incorrectly. Steps he/she took:
Plug in the EV
SECC attempted to start the session
Plug out the EV before it even starts
SECC goes into error.
When the customer tried to plug-in again it after the authentication was provided, he/she couldn't start due to incorrect process.
We must start from PilotState "A" -> "B2" and in both cases we go from "E" -> "B2"
Right before these sessions in DC1, there were 2 other sessions performed that worked perfectly:
And 3h after the failed one also it worked perfectly:
Here I honestly don't see any other reason besides the incorrect usage of the charger.
For the charger 3302, there was a drop of communication on the SECC, this is fixed with the latest v8.0.5, if I have your permission I can download it and install it.
For the unrelated question about the Faulted, I can see in our backend from the past 2 weeks several Door opened errors. If someone was performing tasks on the chargers, this is most likely the root cause, otherwise, we might need to ask someone to go there and make sure that the doors are properly closed.
Let me know what other questions you might have and thank you again for your patience.
Have a nice afternoon.
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: ID0455830-DC/Si-D/IE-[multi] Charging session failed CRM:03056000207
additional_info.body:
Hello Colin,
Thanks for the follow up question.
Let me show you what we send to the backend:
From bottom to top this is what I see:
Door is opened
ChargerOperationMode means that is in Error due to door opened (can be different depending on the situation but it always reports to an error)
EVSE is not ready/secc is offline/modbus0 is not connected are all consequences of the door opened error.
It might be different from every situation, but from the past 2 weeks this is the only scenario I can see.
Let me know if this was what you hoped for.
Thanks!
Best regards,
Francisco
